source_text: πνεύματος καὶ δυνάμεως, οὐχ ὑπ' ἀνθρώπων μόνον καταγγελλόμενον, ἀλλ' ἐξ οὐρανῶν θεόθεν μαρτυρούμενον. 5 Ἐπεὶ τοίνυν ἡμεῖς, οἱ τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ οἰκήτορες, τὸ τοῦ θαύματος παράδοξον αὐταῖς ὄψεσι παραλαβόντες, θεῷ μὲν τῷ παμβασιλεῖ καὶ υἱῷ τῷ μονογενεῖ τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν πρέπουσαν μετ' εὐχαριστίας προσκύνησιν ἀπεδώκαμεν τε καὶ ἀποδώσομεν, εὐχὰς ἐκτενεῖς καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ θεοφιλοῦς σου κράτους ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις τόποις πεποιημένοι τε καὶ ποιησόμενοι, ἔδει δὲ τὰς ἐπουρανίους ταύτας θεοπτίας μὴ παραδοῦναι σιωπῇ, ἀλλ' εὐαγγελίσασθαι σου τὴν ἔνθεον εὐσέβειαν ἐξαυτῆς διὰ τούτων ἐσπούδασα τῶν γραμμάτων· ἵν' ἀγαθῷ θεμελίῳ τῆς παρὰ σοὶ προϋπαρχούσης πίστεως τὴν ἐκ τῶν προσφάτως θεόθεν ἐπιδειχθέντων γνῶσιν ἐποικοδομήσας, βεβαιότερον μὲν τὴν εἰς τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἀναλάβῃς τὴν ἐλπίδα, θαρσῶν δὲ καὶ πασῆς ἀνδρείας συνήθως πεπληρωμένος, ὡς ἂν αὐτὸν θεὸν ἔχων σύμμαχον, τὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ τρόπαιον ἑτοιμότατα προφέρῃς, καύχημα καυχημάτων, τὸ δειχθὲν ἐν οὐρανῷ σημεῖον ἐπαγόμενος· οὗ καὶ τὸ σχῆμα δείξας ἀνθρώποις οὐρανὸς μειζόνως ἐκαυχήσατο. 6 Τὸ μέντοι θαυματούργημα τοῦτο, βασιλεῦ θεοφιλέστατε, προφητῶν μαρτυρίαις καὶ Χριστοῦ φωναῖς ἁγίοις εὐαγγελίοις ἐγκειμέναις ἀκολούθως, ἐτελέσθη τε νῦν καὶ πάλιν μειζόνως τελεσθήσεται· ἐν γὰρ τῷ κατὰ Ματθαῖον εὐαγγελίῳ μελλόντων πραγμάτων γνῶσιν ὁ σωτὴρ τοῖς μακαρίοις ἀποστόλοις αὐτοῦ δωρούμενος καὶ δι' ἐκείνων τοῖς μετ' αὐτοὺς ὁμιλῶν λευκότατα προαναφωνῶν ἔλεγε· "Καὶ τότε φανήσεται τὸ σημεῖον τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν οὐρανῷ".
thought_title: The heavenly sign as divine testimony and call to courage
orientation: Cyril, bishop of Jerusalem, is writing to the emperor Constantius about the cross of light seen over Jerusalem at Pentecost, and now explains why he reports the vision and what it should confirm for the emperor.
pass_a_gloss: of spirit and of power, not being proclaimed by human beings only, but being witnessed from heaven by God. Since therefore we, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, having received the marvel of the wonder with our very eyes, to God the King of all and to the only Son of God we have rendered and will render the fitting worship with thanksgiving, having made and being about to make earnest prayers also for your God-loving might in the holy places, and since it was necessary not to hand over these heavenly visions to silence, but to announce as good news your inspired piety, I have been eager immediately through these letters; so that, having built upon the good foundation of the faith already existing in you the knowledge from the things recently shown from God, you may take up more firmly the hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, and being confident and filled as usual with all courage, as having God himself as ally, you may carry forth most readily the trophy of the cross, a boast of boasts, bringing with you the sign shown in heaven; of which sign heaven, having shown its form to human beings, boasted more greatly. This wonder-working, O most God-loving emperor, in accordance with the testimonies of the prophets and the holy voices of Christ laid down in the gospels, has been accomplished now and will again be accomplished more greatly; for in the gospel according to Matthew, the Savior, granting to his blessed apostles knowledge of things about to be and through them speaking to those after them, proclaiming beforehand most clearly, said: "And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven."

choices.why: The glossary requires 'heavenly vision' for θεοπτία; plural here refers to the multiple aspects of the one vision.
The glossary requires 'piety' for εὐσέβεια, especially of the emperor.
The glossary requires 'trophy' for τρόπαιον, used of the cross as Christ's victory monument.
The glossary requires 'King of all' for παμβασιλεύς as a title for God.
The glossary requires 'only Son' for μονογενής as a title of Christ.
The glossary requires 'sign' for σημεῖον, especially the sign of the Son of Man.

bible_refs.note: καὶ τότε φανήσεται τὸ σημεῖον τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν οὐρανῷ

pass_b_english: of spirit and power—not merely proclaimed by human beings, but witnessed from heaven by God. Since we, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, received this marvel with our own eyes, we have rendered and will render fitting worship with thanksgiving to God the King of all and to the only Son of God, and we have made and will make earnest prayers for your God-loving might in the holy places. It was necessary not to hand these heavenly visions over to silence, but to announce them as good news to your inspired piety at once, and so I have hastened to do through this letter. My purpose is that, building upon the good foundation of the faith already present in you the knowledge of what God has recently shown, you may take up a more secure hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, and that, taking courage and filled as usual with all boldness, since you have God himself as your ally, you may carry forward the trophy of the cross most readily, with the boast of boasts, bearing the sign shown in heaven—the very sign whose shape heaven displayed to human beings and boasted of all the more. This wonder, most God-loving emperor, has now been accomplished in accordance with the testimonies of the prophets and the voices of Christ laid down in the holy Gospels, and it will be accomplished again in greater measure. For in the Gospel according to Matthew, the Savior, granting to his blessed apostles knowledge of things to come and conversing with those after them through them, declared most clearly in advance: “And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven” (Matthew 24:30).

problems.why: The Greek says 'voices of Christ laid down in the holy Gospels', not 'holy words of Christ'; 'voices' (φωναῖς) is the subject, and 'holy' modifies 'Gospels'.
problems.fix: the voices of Christ laid down in the holy Gospels
problems.ruling: Greek says ‘voices of Christ in the holy Gospels’, not ‘holy words of Christ’; shifts subject and genre.

edits.old: the holy words of Christ laid down in the Gospels
edits.new: the voices of Christ laid down in the holy Gospels

fixed: Changed 'holy words of Christ' to 'voices of Christ laid down in the holy Gospels' because the Greek φωναῖς means 'voices' and ἁγίοις modifies εὐαγγελίοις ('holy Gospels'), not the voices.

problems.quote: leading on the boast of boasts, the sign shown in heaven
problems.source_quote: καύχημα καυχημάτων, τὸ δειχθὲν ἐν οὐρανῷ σημεῖον ἐπαγόμενος
problems.why: Greek has 'carrying/leading the sign'; English makes 'boast' the object led, not the sign.
problems.fix: carrying forward the trophy of the cross most readily, with the boast of boasts, the sign shown in heaven going before you
problems.ruling: Greek gives noun phrase “boast of boasts, the sign shown in heaven”; English adds verb “leading on”, altering meaning.

problems.quote: speaking through them to those after them
problems.source_quote: καὶ δι' ἐκείνων τοῖς μετ' αὐτοὺς ὁμιλῶν
problems.why: 'ὁμιλῶν' means 'conversing/associating with', not 'speaking through'; changes how revelation reaches later generations.
problems.fix: and conversing with those after them through them
problems.ruling: ὁμιλῶν means “conversing/associating”, not “speaking through”; English misstates how revelation is conveyed.

edits.old: leading on the boast of boasts, the sign shown in heaven
edits.new: carrying forward the trophy of the cross most readily, with the boast of boasts, the sign shown in heaven going before you

edits.old: speaking through them to those after them
edits.new: conversing with those after them through them

fixed: Fixed 'leading on the boast of boasts, the sign shown in heaven' to 'carrying forward the trophy of the cross most readily, with the boast of boasts, the sign shown in heaven going before you' because the Greek object of 'ἐπαγόμενος' is 'τὸ δειχθὲν ἐν οὐρανῷ σημεῖον' (the sign), not 'καύχημα' (boast).
Fixed 'speaking through them to those after them' to 'conversing with those after them through them' because 'ὁμιλῶν' means conversing or associating with, not speaking through.

problems.quote: with the boast of boasts, the sign shown in heaven going before you
problems.source_quote: καύχημα καυχημάτων, τὸ δειχθὲν ἐν οὐρανῷ σημεῖον ἐπαγόμενος
problems.why: ἐπαγόμενος means 'bearing' or 'carrying', not 'going before you'.
problems.fix: with the boast of boasts, bearing the sign shown in heaven

problems.quote: we have made and will make earnest prayers for your God-loving might in the holy places
problems.source_quote: εὐχὰς ἐκτενεῖς καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ θεοφιλοῦς σου κράτους
problems.why: Greek says the emperor extends prayers, not the author.
problems.fix: you extend earnest prayers for your God‑loving might in the holy places
problems.ruling: Greek εὐχὰς...πεποιημένοι has no expressed subject; context shows 'we' (author/Jerusalemites) as subject throughout, not emperor.

edits.old: with the boast of boasts, the sign shown in heaven going before you
edits.new: with the boast of boasts, bearing the sign shown in heaven

fixed: mistranslation: 'going before you' misreads ἐπαγόμενος, which means 'bearing' or 'carrying'; changed to 'bearing the sign shown in heaven'.

agency: the Greek εὐχὰς ἐκτενεῖς καὶ ὑπὲρ τοῦ θεοφιλοῦς σου κράτους ... πεποιημένοι τε καὶ ποιησόμενοι has the subject 'we' (the inhabitants of Jerusalem) making prayers for the emperor's might; the English 'we have made and will make earnest prayers for your God-loving might' correctly renders this, so no edit was made.

problems.quote: the saving wood of the cross
problems.why: Six different phrases for cross/sign may confuse reader about whether they refer to same object.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'cross' or note these are traditional titles for same object.

variants.text: the saving wood of the cross
the trophy of victory over death
the sign of the Son of Man

problems.why: Four variants of imperial virtue-epithet; reader may not recognize these as formulaic equivalents.
problems.fix: Standardize or footnote that these are conventional honorifics.

problems.quote: building upon the good foundation of the faith already present in you the knowledge
problems.why: Missing preposition or comma makes grammar broken; 'present in you the knowledge' doesn't parse.
problems.fix: Repunctuate: 'already present in you, the knowledge...'

problems.quote: with the boast of boasts, bearing the sign shown in heaven
problems.why: 'boast of boasts' is awkward; likely means 'greatest glory/cause for pride' but sounds like bragging.

problems.quote: the very sign whose shape heaven displayed to human beings and boasted of all the more
problems.why: Heaven 'boasted' is odd personification; Greek likely means heaven gloried in or proclaimed it.

problems.quote: building upon the good foundation of the faith already present in you the knowledge of what God has recently shown
problems.why: Absolute construction without comma or preposition makes sentence ungrammatical as printed.
problems.fix: Insert comma after 'you' or restructure: 'building upon the good foundation of faith already present in you, [add] the knowledge...'

problems.why: Same addressee rendered with varying titles; reader may wonder if different persons are meant.
problems.fix: Use one consistent title or note that all variants address Constantius.

edits.old: building upon the good foundation of the faith already present in you the knowledge of what God has recently shown
edits.new: building upon the good foundation of the faith already present in you, the knowledge of what God has recently shown

fixed: Inserted comma after 'you' to fix the broken grammar in the absolute construction.
Left 'boast of boasts' unchanged: the source has καύχημα καυχημάτων, literally 'boast of boasts', and the English is a faithful rendering.

Changed 'boasted of' to 'gloried in' for heaven's display of the sign: the source has ἐκαυχήσατο, which can mean 'boasted' or 'gloried', and 'gloried in' better conveys the sense of heaven exulting in the sign.
